title: Bevacizumab 10 · colorectal
purpose: To help control bowel cancer that has spread, alongside the chemotherapy chosen by your oncology team.

agents.name: Bevacizumab
agents.explanation: Bevacizumab binds VEGF, a signal that helps new blood vessels grow. It can slow tumour growth but also affect normal blood vessels and wound healing.
visual: Healthy tissues may also be affected
agents.watch: Report bleeding, severe tummy pain, unusual headache or vision changes urgently. Tell the team about any surgery or wound.
risks: Protein in urine and kidney injury
Rare bowel perforation, fistula or serious neurological effects

phases.label: Bevacizumab with chemotherapy
phases.detail: Bevacizumab is given by drip on Day 1 every 14 days with the prescribed fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. Treatment continues while helping and tolerable; there is no fixed total number of cycles. The partner chemotherapy has its own dose days, tests and support plan.

timeline.label: Separate chemotherapy schedule
timeline.text: Use the named partner pack for tablet days, infusions or pump timing

timeline.label: Symptoms and safety checks
timeline.text: Symptoms can occur at any time; attend arranged tests

day_groups.title: Infusion and checks
day_groups.body: Bevacizumab after review; the chemotherapy partner follows its own prescription.
day_groups.action: Confirm blood pressure, urine testing and the full combination plan.

day_groups.title: Between bevacizumab visits
day_groups.body: Follow the separate chemotherapy calendar and report new symptoms promptly.
day_groups.action: Keep arranged checks; contact oncology if unwell.

support.title: Partner chemotherapy
support.text: This covers bevacizumab only. Bring the separate chemotherapy schedule, anti-sickness plan and urgent-contact instructions.

support.title: Blood pressure and urine
support.text: These checks can find problems before you feel unwell. Take blood-pressure medicines as prescribed; do not adjust them yourself.

support.title: Surgery and dental procedures
support.text: Tell oncology before any operation or invasive procedure. The team must agree treatment pauses and assess wound healing.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: Bevacizumab alone does not usually need routine anti-sickness prevention. Chemotherapy partners may need a different plan.

questions.a: Your treating team checks the prescription, tests and symptoms. A completed-cycle stamp records past treatment; it does not authorise the next dose.
Ask the team to update your phase, medicines, test appointments and cycle record. Use the updated prescription.
Your team sets a response and follow-up plan for your cancer and symptoms. This document does not invent a fixed scan or tumour-marker timetable.

context_label: Metastatic colorectal cancer · bevacizumab component with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy
indication_text: NCCP 00212a: bevacizumab with fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy for adults with metastatic carcinoma of the colon or rectum.
schedule_summary: Bevacizumab is given by drip on Day 1 every 14 days with the prescribed fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. Treatment continues while helping and tolerable; there is no fixed total number of cycles. The partner chemotherapy has its own dose days, tests and support plan.
administration_text: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg is given by intravenous infusion in 100 mL sodium chloride 0.9%. The first infusion lasts 90 minutes; the next may be 60 minutes if tolerated, then 30 minutes if tolerated. The full visit also includes checks, preparation, observation and the partner chemotherapy.
monitoring_summary: Bloods, urine protein, blood pressure and cardiac review: Before first treatment; consider heart scan after chest radiation or anthracyclines. Bloods, urine protein and blood pressure: Regular blood/urine tests; BP before each cycle and after treatment. INR if taking warfarin: Weekly until the dose is stable, then before each cycle. Blood pressure, recovery and response scans: BP after treatment; scans and markers follow your individual plan.
urgent_extra: Call your oncology team immediately for coughing blood, significant bleeding, severe tummy pain, sudden breathlessness or chest pain, or a new severe headache, confusion, seizure or vision change. Fever or sudden illness also needs urgent advice, especially with chemotherapy.
consent_support: Discuss the goal, alternatives, important risks for you, fertility/pregnancy prevention, practical support and what would prompt changing or stopping treatment.

chronology_notes.title: Partner treatment changes the schedule
chronology_notes.text: This calendar shows bevacizumab only. Fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy may involve tablets, other infusion days or a home pump. Use its separate written calendar.

chronology_notes.title: Symptoms can occur at any time
chronology_notes.text: Raised blood pressure or protein in urine may have no symptoms. Attend tests, and report bleeding, severe abdominal pain, chest pain, breathlessness or new neurological symptoms promptly.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment decisions
chronology_notes.text: The team may hold or stop bevacizumab for side effects. Decisions for each chemotherapy medicine are separate; do not restart or alter treatment yourself.

timeline_note: Relative days without personal dates. The team confirms actual treatment and test dates.
safety_note: Call your oncology team immediately for coughing blood, significant bleeding, severe tummy pain, sudden breathlessness or chest pain, or a new severe headache, confusion, seizure or vision change. Fever or sudden illness also needs urgent advice, especially with chemotherapy.
passport_visit_note: This is a rolling record, not a six-cycle limit. Record actual doses and interruptions. A stamp records completed treatment and does not authorise the next dose.
anatomy: New severe headache, confusion or visual change needs urgent advice.
Chest pain, sudden breathlessness or a swollen painful leg needs urgent help.
Coughing up blood needs immediate assessment.
Severe tummy pain or a rigid swollen abdomen needs urgent assessment.
Urine tests detect protein; report swelling or much less urine.
Report bleeding and unhealed wounds; tell the team before procedures.

monitoring_schedule.title: My treatment and safety checks
monitoring_schedule.note: Routine safety tests are separate from scans and tumour markers, which follow your individual plan. No universal imaging or tumour-marker interval is specified.

evidence.title: Evidence in this colorectal setting
evidence.intro: The chemotherapy partner, dose schedule and previous treatment determine how trial results apply.
evidence.interpretation: E3200 studied bevacizumab 10 mg/kg every two weeks with FOLFOX4 in metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with a fluoropyrimidine and irinotecan. Adding bevacizumab improved survival in that trial. This does not establish the same result with every chemotherapy partner or predict an individual outcome.

chapters.title: Why bevacizumab is included
chapters.intro: This is one part of your combination treatment.

items.title: Treatment aim
items.text: To help control bowel cancer that has spread, alongside the chemotherapy chosen by your oncology team.

items.title: How it works
items.text: Bevacizumab binds VEGF, a signal that helps new blood vessels grow. It can slow tumour growth but also affect normal blood vessels and wound healing.

items.title: Which evidence applies?
items.text: E3200 studied bevacizumab 10 mg/kg every two weeks with FOLFOX4 in metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with a fluoropyrimidine and irinotecan. Adding bevacizumab improved survival in that trial. This does not establish the same result with every chemotherapy partner or predict an individual outcome.

chapters.title: Before treatment starts
chapters.intro: Some problems are found by tests before symptoms develop.

items.title: Baseline checks
items.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, urine protein, blood pressure and a heart history/examination are checked. A heart ultrasound is considered after chest-wall radiotherapy or previous anthracycline treatment.

items.title: Medicines, wounds and procedures
items.text: Bring all medicines and supplements. Report bleeding, clotting problems, poorly controlled blood pressure, unhealed wounds and planned operations or dental procedures. Oncology must coordinate any treatment pause.

items.title: The complete combination
items.text: Confirm the chemotherapy partner, its tests, infusion or tablet calendar, any pump arrangements and prescribed anti-sickness plan. This bevacizumab pack cannot replace those instructions.

chapters.title: During and between cycles
chapters.intro: Your next dose depends on review, not just the date.

items.title: Blood pressure and urine
items.text: Blood pressure is checked before each cycle and after treatment. Regular blood-count, kidney/liver and urine-protein tests continue. Extra tests are arranged for abnormal results.

items.title: Warfarin
items.text: If taking warfarin, INR is checked weekly until the warfarin dose is stable, then before each cycle. Tell the team about bleeding or any medicine changes.

items.title: Symptoms that need urgent help
items.text: Call your oncology team immediately for coughing blood, significant bleeding, severe tummy pain, sudden breathlessness or chest pain, or a new severe headache, confusion, seizure or vision change. Fever or sudden illness also needs urgent advice, especially with chemotherapy.

items.title: Support medicines
items.text: Bevacizumab alone has minimal sickness risk. The chemotherapy partner determines additional anti-sickness treatment and other supportive medicines; use the issued prescription.

chapters.title: Living with treatment
chapters.intro: Keep information and contacts available on paper as well as online.

items.title: Before any procedure
items.text: Tell every treating clinician that you receive bevacizumab. It can affect wound healing; your oncology team must agree timing around operations and check healing before restarting.

items.title: Keeping a record
items.text: This is a rolling record, not a six-cycle limit. Record actual doses and interruptions. A stamp records completed treatment and does not authorise the next dose.

items.title: Pregnancy and fertility
items.text: Discuss fertility and pregnancy prevention with your team before treatment. Check the duration of contraception and breastfeeding restrictions for every medicine in the combination; contact oncology promptly if pregnancy is possible.

chapters.title: Review and follow-up
chapters.intro: There is no universal final cycle or scan timetable.

items.title: Assessing benefit
items.text: Your consultant sets scans and any tumour-marker tests according to your cancer, symptoms and treatment plan. These are separate from routine blood-pressure and laboratory safety checks.

items.title: After a pause or stopping
items.text: Continue arranged blood-pressure checks and follow-up of unresolved effects. Ask who reviews results, what treatment follows and whom to contact if symptoms develop.
